summary: Kazuharu Mizuno is a scholar in geography and archaeology. He earned a BA at Nagoya University (~1978–1982), a master's at Hokkaido University (~1982–1985), and a DSc at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1985–1990), later becoming a professor at Kyoto University (~2009).

Kazuhiko Atsumi worked in philosophy and other fields. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1954), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991–2000).

Kazuhiko Yoshida studies history, archaeology, Buddhism, and Japanology. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities—the latter under Jay Jasanoff. He held positions at Nagoya City College for Women (~1989–1997), Kyoto University (~1998–2020), and Nagoya City University (2021–2024).

Kazuhiro Furuta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes serving as editor and publisher at the Otani Academic Society (attested 1991) and as dean at Otani University (attested 1998).
Kazuhiro Kawasaki focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Koyasan University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 2005.
Kazuhiro Yamamoto works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

Kazumune Harada researches Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities under Kei Mikogami, Esho Mikogami, Hiroo Kashiwagi, and Makio Takemura. His posts include lecturer at Ryukoku University (1999–2006) and visiting researcher at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2002–2007).
Kazunari Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Sophia University and a master's program at Aichi Gakuin University.

Kazunobu Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied as a graduate student at Otani University. He held positions at Otani University, Kyoto University, the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, and Bukkyo University.

Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, he served as an associate professor at Otani University (~1986–2014) and director at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute (attested 2005–2007).

Kazuo Kano is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Klaus-Dieter Mathes. He held professorships at Koyasan University (~2007–2017) and Komazawa University (~2017).
Kazuo Matsumura works in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976), he held academic posts at Tenri University (~1990–2006) and Wako University (~2006).

Kazuo Okabe was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1958) and the University of Tokyo (~1958–1966). He served as an associate professor and professor at Komazawa University from 1973 until 2006.
Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.
Kazutoshi Soma is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Kazuyoshi Hotta is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and served as an administrator at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo in 1942 and 1946–1948. He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle was a religious studies and history scholar who studied at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown University and served as Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA (~1969–1991).

Kei Kataoka is an Indologist and philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo under Hiroshi Marui. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and became an associate professor at Kyushu University around 2007.
